articles.title: Camarines Norte communities take charge of local climate fight
articles.summary: By arming Camarines Norte residents with climate literacy, they learn to defend their rights and help shape decisions as big solar and wind projects boom across the province

blocks.text: LOCAL LEADERS. The Climate Action Network - Camarines Norte (CANCN) trains student leaders across the Bicol region to spearhead the climate movement, emphasizing collaborative efforts between schools and communities to address local and national climate crises.
CANCN
By arming Camarines Norte residents with climate literacy, they learn to defend their rights and help shape decisions as big solar and wind projects boom across the province

items: Camarines Norte has declared October as Climate Literacy Month to integrate climate education into school curricula and empower local communities against the impacts of climate change.

Local advocates emphasize the importance of grassroots-driven climate empowerment and the need for just transitions to renewable energy, while cautioning against development aggression that threatens rural livelihoods.
The initiative aims to equip residents with climate literacy to actively participate in local energy planning and ensure that developments benefit affected communities.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ALBAY, Philippines – For decades, the provinces along Bicol’s eastern seaboard have stood directly in the path of destructive typhoons, trapping coastal communities in a repetitive cycle of disaster and relief aid.
Now, local organizers and climate advocates in Camarines Norte are striving to end that cycle by placing communities at the center of the solution.

In a landmark initiative for the region, the Climate Action Network – Camarines Norte (CANCN) and Reboot Philippines partnered with multi-sectoral groups to successfully lobby the provincial government into declaring October as Climate Literacy Month.

Adonis Salen II, executive director of CANCN, highlighted how institutionalizing Climate Literacy Month will allow climate education to be integrated directly into school curricula, expanding outreach to local communities through an empowered network of volunteers and partners.
“We believe that literacy is essential to understanding what climate change is, how it impacts us, and how we must respond,” Salen said.

“Through Climate Literacy Month, we have partnered with schools to embed climate education into formal learning, while working with external organizations to bring these critical discussions into local communities.”
He emphasized that this approach goes beyond classroom instruction, fostering open dialogue and raising awareness about the region’s most urgent environmental challenges.

blocks.caption: COMMUNITY POWER. Akbayan Representative Chel Diokno leads a discussion in Camarines Norte on how youth and civic leaders can support a just renewable energy transition through local and national policies. All photos from CANCN

blocks.text: Christian Jay Marmol, secretary and treasurer of CANCN and local communications officer for Reboot Philippines, stressed that Camarines Norte, like much of Bicol, urgently requires grassroots-driven climate empowerment. He noted that strong community mobilization was pivotal in steering the provincial government toward actively supporting local climate advocacy.

“Genuine climate action begins with education and literacy,” Marmol said. “Our partnerships with schools and civil society organizations successfully pushed the provincial government to establish a dedicated Climate Literacy Month — proving that real climate action starts not with solar panels alone, but with the radical democratization of climate knowledge.”
As the first policy of its kind in Bicol, this declaration enables local climate organizations to secure funding and mobilize targeted initiatives alongside the communities they serve.
According to Salen, this can serve as a blueprint for other vulnerable local government units trapped in cycles of relief-aid dependency.

blocks.caption: POLICY VISION. Adonis Salen outlines the policy framework and core agenda behind Camarines Norte’s Climate Literacy Month.

blocks.text: In addition to elevating climate education, local advocates emphasize that the newly established Climate Literacy Month will pave the way for a just transition to renewable energy — a critical priority as energy projects expand across Camarines Norte.
“We are aware that renewable energy projects are increasing in Camarines Norte, so we must remain vigilant against potential development aggression,” Marmol said.

On Saturday, October 24, YHP2 Energy Inc. inaugurated a 10-megawatt solar farm spanning 9.22 hectares in Barangay Bautista, Labo. The facility is set to supply electricity directly to the Camarines Norte Electric Cooperative (CANORECO), delivering locally generated clean power to residents.
Despite these advances, Marmol cautioned that rapid infrastructure development poses significant risks to rural livelihoods.

“When agricultural lands are hastily reclassified as industrial zones for infrastructure projects, it constitutes a form of development aggression against vulnerable farming sectors,” Marmol explained.
“We must ensure that the transition to clean energy remains grounded in justice and protects the communities most affected by these projects.”

blocks.caption: CLIMATE ACTION. Youth and climate leaders convene in Camarines Norte to champion climate literacy as part of their pioneering annual observance of Climate Literacy Month in October.

blocks.text: Beyond solar energy, Camarines Norte is also slated to host a major offshore wind project alongside Camarines Sur.

Spanning the municipalities of Basud and Mercedes, as well as Calabanga, Cabusao, Tinambac, Siruma, and Sipocot in Camarines Sur, the foreign-funded wind farm is projected to generate 1,000 megawatts of electricity. However, the project is expected to impact at least 6,000 small-scale fisherfolk across both provinces.
Such developments come with distinct challenges to rural and coastal livelihoods.

“We are not against these developments because we are advocating for them. Rather, we are ensuring that these kinds of developments are just for the sectors or for the communities affected and that they are included in the consultation,” Marmol added.

blocks.caption: ENERGY LEADERSHIP. Christian Jay Marmol leads the discussion on climate and energy issues and policies during the executive signing event launching Climate Literacy Month.

blocks.text: To prevent further development aggression, Salen stressed that equipping residents with climate literacy is key to helping them defend their rights and actively shape local energy planning.
“While Climate Literacy Month could be seen as a simple observance, we designed it as a platform to advance broader agendas that empower our communities,” Salen said.
“As the government opens doors to the Renewable Energy Roadmap, a climate-literate public will be far better equipped to participate meaningfully as members of the Just Energy Transition Council.”
Beyond the ceremonial signings and policy roadmaps, both Salen and Marmol agree that the true test of Camarines Norte’s Climate Literacy Month lies in its permanence on the ground.

They said that by transforming abstract climate discourse into tangible community power, the province’s residents are proving that when communities are armed with knowledge, they cease to be mere casualties of the climate crisis. – Rappler.com

articles.title: St. Luke’s, NPC investigating data breach on mobile app
articles.summary: The incident may have compromised the personal information of patients and employees, but did not affect hospital operations

blocks.text: The incident may have compromised the personal information of patients and employees, but did not affect hospital operations

MANILA, Philippines – St. Luke’s Medical Center disclosed last Thursday, October 29 that a “data security incident” affected its mobile application. The National Privacy Commission (NPC) also confirmed receipt of a personal data breach notification from St. Luke’s the following day, October 30.

In a statement, St. Luke’s — which has upscale hospitals in Quezon City and Taguig — said it “recently identified unauthorized access to its mobile application, managed by a third-party service provider.”
St. Luke’s announced on Thursday evening that it had made its eHub application unavailable “due to maintenance activities.”
In its October 30 statement, St. Luke’s said it contained the issue after isolating the app, and enlisted third-party cybersecurity experts to investigate what happened.
The incident was said to have potentially affected personal information regarding patients and employees.
The medical center said individuals — patients or employees — whose personal information may have been compromised will be “notified directly.”
It also said that “hospital operations remain unaffected.”
“St. Luke’s sincerely apologizes for any concern this incident may cause and remains committed to protecting the privacy and security of our patients and employees,” it said.
The NPC, meanwhile, said it is “currently reviewing the notification in accordance with established procedures for handling personal data breach notificiations.”

It added that it was unable to disclose further details —such as which application of St. Luke’s was affected by the data breach, the number of patients and employees affected, and the severity of the breach itself – until the NPC completes its evaulation.
We have reached out to St. Luke’s Medical Center’s Data Protection Office for further information and clarifications. We will update this story if we get a response. – Rappler.com

articles.title: DOLE opens '15/30' hotline for workers' labor concerns
articles.summary: The Department of Labor and Employment launched Hotline 15/30, a new 24/7 hotline for workers' concerns, including those related non-compliance with the agency's El Niño guidelines.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 4:05pm

Workers are seen performing their duties at a construction site in Taguig on February 7, 2024. The labor department encourages workers to report non-compliance with El Nino advisories released late-October.
STAR / Ernie Penaredondo
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Labor and Employment launched a round-the-clock hotline for labor and employment concerns on Tuesday, November 3.
Hotline 15/30 — named after workers' semi-monthly pay on the 15th and 30th — replaces the former 1349 service.
DOLE said issues that can be brought to the 1530 hotline include unpaid or delayed wages and benefits, illegal dismissal or termination issues and violations of labor standards, among others.
Employees can also flag workplace safety and health concerns through the hotline, including risks related to extreme heat amid a strong El Niño, according to the department.
Access to the 24/7 hotline is currently limited to PLDT subscribers, but Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino said the department is working to expand services.
DOLE said its 1530 hotline operators will refer the concerns they get to the appropriate DOLE regional or field offices.
Tolentino urged the public to refrain from making prank calls that would distract hotline operators from attending to legitimate concerns.

"Baka mabulunan 'yong linya. Baka 'yong tunay na concerns, lalo (na) 'yong mga riders natin sa El Niño (ay) mahirapang makatawag ... 'Yong mga seryosong mga pangangailangan, lalong lalo na sa workplace: kulang ang ventilation, walang patubig, hindi sumunod sa mga labor advisory tungkol sa El Niño," Tolentino said.

(The lines might get clogged. People with genuine concerns — especially our riders, given the El Niño situation — might find it difficult to get through... There are serious needs, particularly in the workplace: inadequate ventilation, a lack of water supply, and failure to comply with labor advisories regarding El Niño.)
Employers are also allowed to avail of assistance through the hotline, Tolentino added.

The department outlined several advisories in late October to address and manage heat stress during the El Niño period. Included in the advisories are heat index-based guidelines on work arrangements, as well as key protections for delivery riders.
The weather pattern is projected to peak in December 2026 and persist through the first half of 2027.

articles.title: US midterm election: How it works, why it's important and races to watch
articles.summary: US voters are electing a new Congress. The results will be decisive for the future of the United States, and a judgment on Donald Trump's second term as president.

image.caption: Can the Republicans hang on to their majority in Congress?Image: Blake Fagan/AFP

blocks.text: On November 3, United States citizens will vote in the midterm elections. These won't decide who gets to sit in the White House; instead, Americans will be voting on who they want to see in the Capitol.

Midterm elections are held every four years, at the exact halfway point between presidential elections. The people of the United States decide who will represent them in the two chambers of the US Congress, the House of Representatives and the Senate. Some states are also voting for their governor. These are the decisions on the ballot paper — but they are not the only thing voters will be taking into account.

J. Miles Coleman, an election analyst at the Center for Politics at the University of Virginia, explained before the last midterms that they were "often a referendum on the president and party currently in power." If the people are content, the party of the leader in the White House does better than if the people are predominantly dissatisfied. President Donald Trump's approval ratings are currently at a record low.

blocks.caption: President Donald Trump's approval ratings have sunk to an all-time low: More than 60% of Americans view him negativelyImage: Jacquelyn Martin/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Who are Americans electing in the midterms?

All the seats in the US House of Representatives are up for election. Its 435 members are elected by eligible voters across the country. Each member represents one electoral district. These are allocated based on population size. As a result, relatively large US states where few people live, such as Wyoming, have only one seat in the House of Representatives. New Jersey, a much smaller state by surface area but with a larger population, has 12. Representatives are elected for a two-year term of office.

US senators, on the other hand, are elected for a six-year term. The Senate, the other chamber of the US Congress, has 100 seats: two for each of the 50 US states, regardless of size. Around one third of these senatorial seats come up for election every two years. This year there are 35, meaning that not every state will be electing a senator in these midterms.

Separately, voters in 36 states will elect their governor, whose term of office is four years in most states. Many decisions in the US are taken at state level, on everything from abortion law to education and electoral procedure. It can therefore make a considerable difference to people's lives whether Democrats or Republicans are the ones making these decisions in their state.
Who currently has a majority in the US Congress?
At present, the Republicans, the party of President Trump, have a majority in both houses of Congress — but its margin is slim.

The House of Representatives currently has 218 Republican deputies, 214 Democrats, and one independent, who usually votes with the Republicans. Two seats are vacant. Observers think it likely that the Democrats will seize the majority in this chamber in the upcoming elections. "It would be a surprise if the Democrats don't at least take the House [of Representatives]," Coleman told the American broadcaster CBS at the end of October.

In the Senate there are currently 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats, and two independent senators who usually vote with the Democrats. When a vote in the Senate is deadlocked 50:50, the US vice president has the deciding vote. This means that currently, Trump's Vice President JD Vance would tip the scales if there were a tie in a Senate vote.

blocks.caption: Republicans and Democrats are vying for seats in the two chambers of the US CongressImage: Graeme Sloan/Sipa USA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Why are the midterms so important?

Voter turnout is typically lower for midterms than for presidential elections, but the results will decisively influence US politics for the next few years. Despite the significant executive power delegated to the presidency, the majority of federal political decisions have to be approved by Congress before they can be implemented.

It is therefore considerably easier for Trump to govern the country as he chooses if the Republicans have a majority in both chambers of Congress. If the Democrats win a majority in one or both chambers, it will be more difficult for him to make changes to either domestic or foreign policy.
Which races are crucial?

The Democrats only need to win four more seats in the House of Representatives to gain a majority. They would then have 218 representatives. Out of the 435 races, only a few are still considered toss-ups. These include districts in Iowa, Virginia and Montana.

One senatorial race to watch is the one in Texas. Current polls put Democrat James Talarico level with his Republican rival, Ken Paxton. The Democrats need four more seats in the Senate to win a majority. The possibility that Texas could be one of them is already a sensation. No Democrat has won here at state level since 1994. Talarico now even has the support of some members of the Bush family, the Texas Republican dynasty of former presidents George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush, his son.
Many US voters are undecided, disillusioned or disengaged

In the gubernatorial elections it is possible that, for the first time in US history, a Black woman could become state governor. In Minnesota, the Democrat Amy Klobuchar and the Black Republican Lisa DeMuth are vying for the position, while in Georgia the Black Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is up against the Republican Rick Jackson.

DeMuth is unlikely to win in Minnesota: The state generally votes Democrat, and Klobuchar, who has been state senator there for almost two decades, is much better known than her rival. In Georgia, however, the latest polls suggest it's neck-and-neck. Bottoms has a realistic chance of winning.
This article has been translated from German.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 3:50pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Tuesday said a total of 80 Chinese vessels were monitored at a number of key features in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) in October 2026.
The figure is lower compared to the 101 Chinese ships seen in the disputed area in September 2026.

In an update, AFP spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) and China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels were seen in WPS features from October 1 to 31:
• Ayungin Shoal – 11 CCGs, 13 PLANs
•Bajo de Masinloc – 30 CCGs, 11 PLANs
• Escoda Shoal – three CCGs, eight PLANs
• Pag-asa Islands – three CCGs, one PLAN

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as the West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within, and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: DA, civil society groups find coordinate discrepancies in 8 of 1,669 proposed 2027 FMR projects
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture (DA) has tightened its review of project documents, including those for farm-to-market roads (FMRs), to prevent errors in project information.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 3:37pm
The Department of Agriculture (DA) has tightened its review of project documents, including those for farm-to-market roads (FMRs), to prevent errors in project information.

Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. ordered a comprehensive review of project descriptions, supporting documents, and validation procedures after senators flagged errors in the coordinates of proposed FMR projects for 2027 submitted by the agency.
“We are reviewing the data and working with civil society groups to make sure the technical descriptions are accurate and verifiable,” he said in a statement on Tuesday.

“If there are errors in the technical descriptions, whether typographical or otherwise, we will take responsibility and correct them. Public funds must go to the projects they are intended for,” Tiu Laurel added.

The DA said it immediately coordinated with the People's Budget Coalition, Bisto Proyekto.ph, and the Bureau of Agriculture and Fisheries Engineering to address discrepancies traced to typographical errors.
The DA and civil society groups identified coordinate discrepancies in eight of the 1,669 entries for proposed FMR projects.
"Upon close inspection, it showed one or two numbers in the coordinate were mistyped from the correct coordinates," the DA said.
Tiu Laurel also ordered improvements in geotagging, internal reviews, and third-party validation of project documents.
The DA maintains an online portal for transparency and monitoring of FMR projects nationwide at fmrwatch.bafe.gov.ph.
“Public funds must be backed by accurate project information. That is our accountability to Congress, our farmers and fisherfolk, and the Filipino people,” Tiu Laurel said.
Under the proposed P198.45-billion budget for the DA in 2027, P16 billion is earmarked for FMR projects. This is half the P33 billion allocated for the program in the 2026 budget.
Since President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. assumed office in 2022, a total of 537 FMR projects have been completed, the Department of Agrarian Reform earlier said.
These projects cover a combined distance of 435.807 kilometers and benefit 155,123 agrarian reform beneficiaries (ARBs). —VBL, GMA News

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalate as the powerful militia advances towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz

DUBAI, UAE – Talks between Iran and Saudi Arabia are ongoing as Tehran aims to reach new regional security arrangements for countries in the region without foreign military involvement, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on X on Tuesday, November 3.

Last week, top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran, the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations since August. The US-Israeli war on Iran started in late February and since then, fighting has spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

Riyadh said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to “prevent the return of military escalation,” as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis had intensified in recent weeks.

Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated as the powerful militia advanced towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping chokepoint that lies on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz.
The Houthis have also attacked Saudi oil facilities and airports including Riyadh’s international airport, disrupting flights and oil exports and drawing Saudi airstrikes on Yemen in response.
Impoverished Yemen has been mired in a civil war since the Houthis pushed the internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government out of the capital, Sanaa, in 2014. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
articles.summary: An impasse between the US and Russia at the UN means its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years.

blocks.text: Western Sahara, on Africa's north-west coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast.
As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory.
The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination.

Morocco's then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975 about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain.

Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the question of sovereignty.
The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control.
Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario.
Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso's mandate.
In Laayoune, the territory's largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI.

"The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute," Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC.
He said Morocco would now have more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence towards autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.
The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara's legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.
Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).
But the decision comes after several countries backed the position of Morocco, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim a central part of its foreign policy.
In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.
France also backed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute in 2024.
The fear is that Minurso's departure could lead to renewed fighting.
The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation.
Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians.
Laaroussi admits that the mission's departure could create security gaps.
"Minurso's departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment," he says.
The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online.
Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara.

In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country's claim to sovereignty over the territory.
Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it "within respect of its security and sovereignty."
Polisario has not said what it will do next.
Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high.

According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver.
Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco's $6.3bn.

articles.title: 'Walang pasok' powers amid site-specific conditions given to schools by Marcos EO
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order (EO) that gives schools an authority to independently declare onsite class suspensions during bad weather or hazardous conditions. Under…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 3:20pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has signed an executive order (EO) that gives schools an authority to independently declare onsite class suspensions during bad weather or hazardous conditions.
Under EO No. 130, schools can impose granular suspension even when there is no suspension declared by national or local government.

“In the absence of an applicable automatic suspension or localized suspension declared by the concerned LCE (local chief executive), an educational institution or learning center may, through its duly authorized official, declare granular suspension, in coordination with the concerned LCE, upon the determination that an actual or imminent threat to the safety, health, or welfare of learners and personnel exists based on documented site-specific conditions,” the EO read.

Aside from granular suspension, schools may automatically suspend onsite classes and work upon issuance by PAGASA, PHIVOLCS, DENR-Environmental Management Bureau of any warning, advisory, alert level, and forecasts.
Moreover, local officials may declare suspensions based on the specific, verified disaster or risk levels within their respective city, municipality, or province.
However, the EO provides that schools should implement learning continuity measures despite the suspension of in-person classes or activities.

“Educational institutions and learning continuity measures consistent with the policies of the ECCD Council, DepEd, CHED TESDA, and other agencies operating or supervising specialized educational institutions and learning centers, to ensure that learning continues despite the suspension of in-person classes,” it read.

Further, EO No. 130 also allows individual schools to seek the early resumption of classes ahead of an LGU-wide order, provided a documented site-specific assessment proves the school grounds are safe and the local mayor or governor concurs.

Amid the threat of El Nino, the Department of Education said a school can suspend both physical and online classes once the local temperature hits 42 degrees Celsius, upon coordination with the concerned local government.

articles.title: Schools may reopen during LGU class suspensions under new Marcos order
articles.summary: Schools will be allowed to resume in-person classes even while a mayor's or governor's class suspension is still in force, under an executive order signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 3:13pm

Students walk across the gutter-deep flood along the corner of Taft and UN Avenues in Manila following a heavy downpour brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon on Monday, July 21, 2025. The city of Manila on Monday suspended classes at all levels in public and private schools starting at 12 noon.
The STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — Schools will be allowed to resume in-person classes even while a mayor's or governor's class suspension is still in force, under an executive order signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that updates rules on calling off classes during disasters.

Executive Order 130, signed on October 28 and originally proposed by the Department of Education (DepEd), lets a school reopen earlier than a city- or province-wide suspension if an assessment shows its campus is safe and accessible, and the local chief executive concurs.
The new order replaces Executive Order 66 of 2012, signed under former President Benigno Aquino III.
The order recognizes a need to "rationalize and harmonize" the different rules governing the suspension of in-person classes and on-site government work.
EO 130 covers all public and private schools and learning centers, including colleges and technical-vocational schools.
What is new
EO 130 spells out three kinds of suspensions:

items: Automatic suspensions, triggered without "need of further declaration," upon the issuance of a warning, alert level or forecast by PAGASA, PHIVOLCS, and other relevant government agencies. These are based on "prescribed technical thresholds" to be detailed in later guidelines.
Localized suspensions, which can be decided by the local chief executive in the absence of an applicable automatic suspension, based on local risk assessments.

Granular suspensions, which are suspensions called by the school itself in the absence of the first two kinds. This is done "in coordination" with the local chief executive and upon the "determination" of an actual or imminent threat to the safety, health or welfare of students and personnel. DepEd gave public school heads similar authority in 2024.

blocks.text: The executive order stated that schools can also, in turn, decide to resume classes on their own during a local suspension with a documented site assessment and the concurrence of the mayor or governor.
This option applies only to localized suspensions declared by local officials, not to those triggered automatically by hazard warnings.
Local chief executives also must now name the areas a suspension covers, down to barangays and, where practicable, individual schools, and state how long it will last.
They are to consult barangay captains, the schools division superintendent and private school heads as needed.
Classes resume once a suspension lapses or a warning is lifted, downgraded or expires, but only after required safety inspections.
The order also states that suspending in-person classes "shall not automatically suspend learning."
Schools must shift to alternative delivery where feasible, and staff to alternative work arrangements.

The order no longer spells out which grade levels are to suspend in-person instruction under each storm signal. Previously, EO 66 called off preschool under Signal No. 1, classes up to high school under Signal No. 2, and all levels and government work under Signal No. 3 or higher.
Those thresholds will instead be set in guidelines that DepEd must issue within 30 days of the order taking effect.

articles.title: Americans head to polls in midterm elections seen as referendum on Trump
articles.summary:
Control of the Senate and House of Representatives, both currently held by the Republicans, is at stake

Americans are heading to the polls today in US midterm elections widely seen as a…

blocks.text: Americans are heading to the polls today in US midterm elections widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second presidency and a chance for opponents to rein in his untrammeled power.

Democrats and Republicans have scrambled in recent days to deliver their final pitches to voters with control of the US Senate and House of Representatives – both currently held by the Republicans – at stake.

The campaign has been overshadowed by Trump, who has staged several dozen rallies across the country while urging his make America great again (Maga) base to vote for Republican candidates and pretend his name was on the ballot.

The party holding the White House typically loses congressional seats at midterm elections and Democrats are hoping Trump’s nose-diving popularity can be exploited to generate a “blue wave” groundswell of popular opposition that will win them both the Senate and the House.

They are seeking to wrest control over both chambers of Congress to put a brake on Trump’s presidential power, which has gone largely unchecked as he has launched a fierce immigration crackdown involving mass arrests and deportations, waged war on Iran, imposed tariffs on foreign imports , and embarked on vainglorious building projects, including a White House ballroom.

Opinion surveys have suggested the Democrats are well-positioned to win the House. The party faces a tougher task to regain control of the Senate, although it has targeted several Republican-held seats including Ohio, Texas and Maine.

A final set of polls from the New York Times and Siena University, published on Sunday, put Democratic candidates ahead in five of seven key battleground contests – including Texas and Kansas, where voters have not sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1988 and 1932, respectively.

The final stretch of the campaign was not without drama for the Democrats, however. In Michigan – widely seen as a crucial pillar to either party’s ambitions of control in the Senate – Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost her party’s senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed his Republican rival, Mike Rogers, on Sunday.

Stevens was widely condemned by fellow Democrats over the move, which followed a feud with the El-Sayed campaign over an outside group’s campaign ad that blamed the high cost of living on US support for Israel. Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, described her endorsement of Rogers as “a despicable betrayal”.
“Whatever they’re trying to distract you, it’s because they’re picking your pocket,” El Sayed told hundreds of supporters in Royal Oak, Michigan on Monday.

The extraordinary rupture in Michigan took places days after the party faced damaging headlines in Alaska, where it was reported that the Democratic senate candidate’s campaign was behind an effort to recruit a challenger with almost the same name as her rival, the Republican senator Dan Sullivan. (The Democratic candidate, Mary Peltola, has denied any knowledge of such a scheme on the part of her campaign.)

Before the report of the Peltola campaign’s involvement, the Department of Justice (DoJ) filed a lawsuit to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate results in the event of a Republican defeat, citing potential “voter confusion” over the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot. The lawsuit has since been dismissed by a judge.

Trump has put himself center stage by crisscrossing the country to deliver a succession of speeches for Republican candidate, despite opinion polls showing his approval ratings falling to record lows of between 33 and 37%.

Democrats have sought to reinforce the message that the election is about Trump while trying to highlight the perceived corruption of the US president and his family, along with affordability issues, and the impact of the conflict with Iran, which is seen as having exacerbated the cost of living.

Opinion surveys have shown that voters have become increasingly concerned about corruption in government. A recent Harris poll for the Guardian found that 76% think elected officials care more about enriching themselves than improving the economy for ordinary people.
Disclosures to the US office of government ethics show that Trump has earned about $2.2bn since returning to the White House, including royalties from his own name-branded meme coin.
As the president has grown wealthier, voters have chafed under rising living costs, which Trump vowed to reduce during his 2024 presidential campaign.

The war with Iran – which Trump launched last February in tandem with Israel – has stoked inflation by increasing global oil prices, which has led to higher prices at the pump for American motorists and raised the cost of diesel, a vital fuel for supply chains and farmers.
The US elections also take place under a shadow of uncertainty about whether Trump will accept the results if they do not go the Republicans’ way.

Alaska is just one of the cases pursued by the justice department – under the control of Trump’s close ally, Todd Blanche, the attorney general – that opponents say are designed to cast doubt on the election’s integrity, including through baseless claims of mass voting by non-US citizens.
The justice department plans to deploy a record 1,000 election monitors to polling stations across the US. Critics have denounced the move as voter intimidation.

articles.title: Australia’s social media ban ‘ill-thought-out’, Reddit argues in high court challenge
articles.summary:
Reddit challenges ban on grounds it impinges implied freedom of political communications for teens

  • Get our

blocks.text: The Australian government’s rush to pass the under-16s social media ban legislation in 2024 led to “ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation” that has since been narrowed after Reddit sued the government, lawyers for the social media company told the high court on Tuesday.
Reddit, one of the top 10 websites visited in the world, has challenged the teen social media ban on the grounds it impinges the implied freedom of political communication for under-16s.

In oral arguments before the high court on Tuesday, Reddit’s counsel, Perry Herzfeld SC, argued in the years leading up to the ban legislation, a 2021 parliamentary inquiry on social media had not recommended introducing a ban, with the eSafety commissioner warning the inquiry at the time it would be a “blunt force approach”.
When the government announced the ban in 2024, Reddit argued the legislation was introduced and passed within a week, with only 24 hours of submissions allowed.
“A process of this kind is likely to lead to ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation,” Herzfeld argued.

After eSafety announced Reddit would be included in the ban, and Reddit did not accept it met the definition of a social media platform under the law, the company announced the high court challenge to the law in late 2025.

In March this year, the communications minister, Anika Wells, introduced new rules as part of the legislation that defines additional requirements for social media companies to meet the definition including logged-in features, recommendation features or endless scroll.

Herzfeld argued the ban does not address those factors specifically by a broad ban on under-16s accounts, and has argued it would be able to under different legislation – pointing to the digital duty of care legislation currently before the parliament.
Outside the court, Wells told reporters she wasn’t the minister at the time the legislation passed, but said the government’s arguments in response would be made in court.
Since the ban came into effect in December last year, more than 5 million user accounts the platforms understand belong to people aged under 16 across 10 platforms have been suspended or deactivated.
The platforms currently covered by the ban include Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads.

The case centres around whether the effect of the ban limiting political communications is justified by what the government has said is a “credible risk” of harms such as mental health issues, sleeping problems and eating disorder issues.
Politically engaged teens

Herzfeld told the court on Tuesday the ban prevents teenagers from actively engaging in political communications through subreddits such as r/Australia. While they can still view the content without an account, they can’t make their own posts, comment or upvote content, Reddit argued.

Justice Jacqueline Gleeson expressed reservations when pointed to examples of high-profile teens being politically engaged in social media – such as 6News’ Leo Puglisi, who began his news site at the age of 11.
Gleeson said the “vast majority of teens the vast majority of time” do not engage in politics while under 16.

When asked whether teens were being limited in engaging in political communication on just those platforms covered by the ban, Herzfeld argued the platforms offer teens a much wider audience compared with “shouting on the street” or being interviewed in the media.

Herzfeld said the Australian government had also cited a number of studies in its submissions outlining the “credible risks” of harm that the ban is aiming to address, but none of the studies cited had mentioned Reddit. He conceded Reddit was not arguing the parliament had to wait for scientific consensus on the link between the harmful design features of social media and the harms.
after newsletter promotion

At the end of its argument on Tuesday, Reddit outlined a number of alternatives the government could have pursued, including the digital duty of care bill currently before the parliament, as well as laws prohibiting push notifications, or limiting the time children can spend on the platform, or requiring child accounts to only be allowed with parental control.
Maximising engagement

Government barrister Joanna Davidson SC, told the court the design features outlined in the rules, which she said are designed to maximise engagement on the platforms, are “broadly shared” across all 10 platforms, including Reddit.
Those features include autoplay video, recommendation systems, notifications by default and surfacing the most popular content.
Davidson said the platforms encourage users to stay to maximise user engagement and bring in more revenue. Those features can have a “compounding” risk of harm when working together.
When people keep returning to social media for fear of missing out, it can lead to issues such as a lack of sleep, or an increased likelihood of depression, she said.
Children are more vulnerable to the risks due to their cognitive stage of development, Davidson said.
The government will continue to make its argument on Wednesday.

The Digital Freedom Project, led by New South Wales Libertarian MP John Ruddick, adopted Reddit’s arguments against the law, and only sought to be heard on the issue of whether as a group advocating for its members it had standing to bring the case.
The court heard the group had “at least one” member aged between 13 and 15 who was affected by the ban.

Ruddick was joined outside the court this morning by the original plaintiff for the case – 16-year-old Noah Jones – and his mother, Renee, as well as One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts. Jones and fellow teen Macey Nyland withdrew as plaintiffs in the case due to the legal cost risk if the case went against them.

articles.title: LTFRB fines Move It P555-M after exceeding motorcycle taxi rider limit
articles.summary: The transport regulator fines Move It P10,000 per excess rider, which it says reached 55,575 riders as of May 2026

blocks.text: MOTORCYCLE TAXI. Riders of Move It form a motorcade.
Move It Facebook Page
The transport regulator fines Move It P10,000 per excess rider, which it says reached 55,575 riders as of May 2026

MANILA, Philippines – Move It onboarded 55,575 motorcycle taxi riders beyond its government-approved limit, according to an investigation by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB).
Move It was authorized to have only 17,746 riders in Metro Manila, Cebu City, and Cagayan de Oro City, but had a total of 73,321 as of May 2026, exceeding its allocation by 55,575, the LTFRB found.
In a decision dated October 9, the LTFRB fined Move It P555.75 million, equivalent to P10,000 for each excess rider.
The LTFRB also cited Move It’s report of 147,214 active rider-partners in Metro Manila. Of these, 44,164 operated for more than eight hours daily, while 103,050 operated for fewer than eight hours.
The agency said Move It’s defense was not that it complied with its rider allocation, but that only certain categories of riders should count toward the excess.

The LTFRB maintained that Move It was aware of its regulatory obligations, including keeping its rider population within its authorized allocation and reporting all rider activations, deactivations, and reactivations.
The agency also said Move It should have gradually reduced its rider population through right-sizing measures and stopped onboarding additional riders.
LTFRB, however, clarified on Tuesday, November 3, that its decision is not yet final because Move It filed a motion for reconsideration.

“What the agency is focused on is addressing the plight of the thousands of overboarded riders who invested their own resources to earn a decent living – and whose only fault was that they acted in good faith and trusted that they were allowed to operate under the existing rules and regulations,” the LTFRB said.
The agency said it is developing measures to address the situation of affected riders while ensuring that motorcycle taxi platforms comply with government regulations on rider onboarding.

In April 2026, the government’s cash aid rollout program exposed discrepancies between the number of motorcycle taxi drivers operating on the ground and those reported by ride-hailing firms. –Rappler.com

articles.title: St. Luke's Medical Center probing cybersecurity incident on mobile app
articles.summary: Private healthcare provider St. Luke's Medical Center has said it is investigating a "cybersecurity incident" that it detected on its mobile application.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 2:27pm
Private healthcare provider St. Luke's Medical Center has said it is investigating a "cybersecurity incident" that it detected on its mobile application.

In a statement issued Monday, the company said, "On October 29, 2026, St. Luke's Medical Center identified a cybersecurity incident affecting a portion of the platform that supports our mobile application, which is managed by a third-party service provider."
St. Luke's did not specify the extent of a potential data exposure, but assured that critical patient data records are intact.

"Our Electronic Medical Records (EMR) and other core clinical systems are unaffected. The EMR is the heart of our patient information, holding the records our team relies on to care for our patients," the statement read.
The healthcare provider added that it carried out immediate mitigation protocols and reported the matter to National Privacy Commission.

"Upon detection, we immediately initiated containment and remediation measures. The affected platform was isolated and secured, and the mobile app was taken offline. We engaged independent cybersecurity experts to conduct a comprehensive forensic investigation and to further strengthen our security safeguards," it added.
St. Luke's said it is currently notifying people whose personal information may have been affected. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: PNP: No shoot-to-kill order vs Bato dela Rosa
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday denied reports that it had issued a shoot-to-kill order against Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 2:26pm
The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday denied reports that it had issued a shoot-to-kill order against Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa.

“May I remind the public that only share or believe information coming from verified and official sources. Wala pong shoot-to-kill order na inilabas,” PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co told reporters in an interview.
(May I remind the public that only share or believe information coming from verified and official sources. No shoot-to-kill order has been issued.)
Co pointed out that the PNP would carry out its operations against Dela Rosa within the bounds of the law.
In a separate statement, PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. also stressed that the police do not subscribe to a shoot-to-kill approach in serving arrest warrants.

“The PNP does not subscribe to a shoot-to-kill approach. Our mandate is to enforce the law, not to take the law into our own hands. Every operation must be guided by due process, respect for human rights, and the rule of law,” Nartatez said.
All operations must observe maximum restraint, proportionality, and respect for human rights, according to the PNP.
Due process
This came after Cagayan de Oro 1st District Representative Lordan Suan denied social media posts falsely attributing to him a supposed call for a shoot-to-kill resolution against Dela Rosa.
“It has come to my attention that several social media pages are amplifying a false and malicious statement falsely attributed to me,” Suan earlier said in a Facebook post on Monday.

“The quote circulating online claiming I threatened a House hearing and a ‘shoot-to-kill’ resolution against Senator Ronald ‘Bato’ dela Rosa is FALSE, FAKE, FABRICATED. I never made that statement. I stand firmly for due process and the rule of law,” he added.
Dela Rosa is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the crimes against humanity case arising from former President Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs.
The senator is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes.

Earlier, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) claimed that Dela Rosa was hiding in Mindanao under the protection of an “armed and powerful group,” but did not identify the group.
A P50-million reward is being offered for information that would lead to the senator’s arrest.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 2:21pm
The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) has approved a minimum wage hike in Western Visayas and SOCCSKSARGEN, which will be implemented in November.
According to Manny Vargas' report on Super Radyo DZBB,there is a P40 to P45 increase for minimum wages in Western Visayas, which will be effective on November 19.
From P550, this will raise the current minimum wage to P590 a day for workers in non-agriculture, industrial and commercial establishments with more than 10 employees

For establishments with less than 10 employees, their new minimum wage would be P565 a day from P525. This is also the same new wage rate for agriculture workers, who had previously been at P520 a day.
Household helpers will also receive an additional P500 a month, which raises their monthly minimum salary to P7,000.
Meanwhile, the DOLE also announced a wage hike in SOCCSKSARGEN.
The prevailing minimum wage for the region is P443 to P460. There will be an additional P41 a day, which will be implemented in two tranches.
The first tranche, P16 a day, will be implemented on November 19. This will raise the SOCCSKSARGEN minimum wage to P459 a day for agriculture workers, and P476 a day for non-agriculture workers.
The second tranche, P25 a day, will be implemented on January 1, 2027. This would again raise the region’s minimum wage to P484 for agriculture workers, and P501 for non-agriculture workers.
DOLE also announced a P450 monthly raise for household helpers starting November 19, which raises their total monthly wage to P6,450. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Budget watchdogs urged to report 'red flags' to Palace
articles.summary: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Tuesday urged civil society organizations (CSOs) to report “red flags” in the proposed 2027 national budget to Malacañang to help President…

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 2:01pm

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Tuesday urged civil society organizations (CSOs) to report “red flags” in the proposed 2027 national budget to Malacañang to help President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. review it before signing.

“Sa mga nagbabantay ng budget, kung meron kayong kopya na inyong nakita at napansin na red flag, ipagbigay-alam niyo lang po sa amin, bigyan niyo kami ng kopya, mismo ang PCO dahil kakailanganin din po ito ng Pangulo,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said during a press briefing.
(To those who are watching the budget, if you have a copy where you see a red flag, just let us know, give the Presidential Communications Office a copy because the President will also need it.)
Castro added that Malacañang is also willing to conduct a meeting with SCOs to assess the 2027 national budget.
The People's Budget Coalition (PBC) has cautioned against over a trillion pesos worth of “red flags” under the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget for fiscal year 2027.
PBC co-convenor AJ Montesa said that under the 2027 budget, P210 billion was ‘soft pork’ in the form of patronage-driven financial assistance.
Meanwhile, P695 billion was ‘hard pork,’ which consists of politicized infrastructure projects; and P112 billion in ‘shadow pork,’ or unprogrammed appropriations.
Castro said the President would not intervene with Congress' work due to the separation of power, but asked not to reduce the proposed budget to ensure that the projects are not delayed.

“Ang proyekto na nakasaad sa proposed budget, huwag na bawasan dahil matitigil o magiging sanhi ito para ma-delay ang mga proyektong dapat natapusin sa administrasyon ni Pangulong Marcos Jr.,” Castro said.
(The projects included in the proposed budget should not be reduced, as doing so could halt or delay projects that are meant to be completed during the administration of President Marcos Jr.)
She also warned government officials against making insertions in the budget.
“Ang pondo ng bayan hindi dapat inaabuso. Ang pondo ng bayan ay dapat sa taong-bayan, hindi sa bulsa ng ninuman,” she said.
(Public funds should not be abused. It should go to the people, not into the pockets of anyone.)

“Hindi papayagan ng Pangulo ang anumang budget amendments kung ito ay walang sapat na dokumento, walang tamang deskripsiyion at walang kahihinatnan ng proyekto. Hindi yan papayagan ng Pangulo,” she added.
(The President will not allow any budget amendments that lack sufficient documentation, proper descriptions, or clear project outcomes. The President will not permit that.)

Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito earlier committed to inviting CSOs to observe the bicameral conference committee deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for fiscal year 2027.

Meanwhile, Senator Panfilo Lacson said the majority bloc is supporting efforts to remove questionable allocations from the proposed 2027 budget and ensure transparency in the budget-making process. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Denmark pushes for EU ban on ‘turbo chickens’ as secret footage causes outrage
articles.summary:
Minister says government will work towards banning fast-growing breed across country and throughout EU

The Danish government is pursuing a national ban on “turbo chickens” and is calling for…

blocks.text: The Danish government is pursuing a national ban on “turbo chickens” and is calling for the fast-growing breed to be prohibited across Europe.
The move comes amid widespread outrage over allegations of lawbreaking by one of Denmark’s big chicken producers.

According to a TV2 documentary broadcast last week, producer Christian Tvergaard broke Danish law by giving chickens only half the amount of darkness per day that is required, in order to encourage them to eat more. The documentary featured secretly filmed footage from a chicken coop in North Jutland.

The Ross 308 breed, labelled the turbo chicken, is the most widespread in Danish poultry production. It grows from about 50 grams to 2kg in just 33 days. Such rapid growth can lead to problems with the animal’s bones and organs. Other chicken breeds take between 46 and 63 days to reach the same weight.

Denmark’s minister for nature and animal welfare, Christian Rabjerg Madsen, said he discouraged Danes from buying turbo chickens, telling the broadcaster: “I want to work for a national ban. But it’s clear that this is something that needs to be investigated both legally and economically.”
He added: “Now we will work for a national ban, we will work for a ban at EU level.”
In response to the documentary, Tvergaard has admitted to making some wrong decisions.
He told TV2: “I look inward and must admit that I have made some wrong decisions. There is no excuse for that, but I can learn from it and correct where I have not done well enough.
“And I have done that, both when it comes to the lighting programme and a number of the workflows we have in the stable, where both procedures and the roster have been tightened up.”

The proposal for the ban on turbo chickens is gaining political momentum and attracting cross-party support in Denmark. But industry figures warn that to be effective, any ban must include imported chickens as well.

Klement Hinkbøl Ribergaard, the chief executive of chicken producer Danpo, said: “If Denmark alone bans the production of fast-growing chickens while shops, restaurants and consumers in the Danish market can continue to buy imported, fast-growing chicken of more or less questionable quality, we risk a situation in which animal welfare certainly does not benefit.”

With fast-growing breeds so prominent across the EU, it would mark a landmark shift. According to Eurogroup for Animals, 95% of chickens in the bloc are now raised in intensive systems and bred to produce the cheapest amount of meat possible, creating a “race to the bottom”.

“Fast-growing breeds are inherently predisposed to suffering, with their bodies growing so quickly they can barely stand on their legs,” said Reineke Hameleers, the advocacy group’s chief executive. “Denmark’s political willingness to stop this is an example that should be followed by the EU, for it presents the progressiveness this industry needs, one that is backed up by scientific evidence.”

Britta Riis, chief executive of Animal Protection Denmark, said turbo chickens were the result of a “deeply unethical and grotesque form of breeding” that led to “systematic abuse” and considerable suffering for the birds. The organisation is calling for all chickens to be bred for the same amount of time as organic breeds, which is 56 days.

Animal welfare has featured heavily in public debate in recent months in Denmark. The issue of pig farming dominated the last general election to such an extent that it was nicknamed the “pig election”.
The country is due to stop mink farming by August 2029 after the current government decided not to seek an EU exemption on the practice.

articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying
articles.summary:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were…
articles.byline: Patrick Greenfield, Elisângela Mendonça and Phoebe Weston

blocks.text: British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.

This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
Documents obtained by the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay under the UK’s Freedom of Information Act reveal Vantara’s efforts to lobby British officials and ministers before the meeting.

Ambani, 31, is the heir to the oil and gas fortune of one of India’s richest men, Mukesh Ambani. He set up a 1,400-hectare (3,500-acre) private zoo near his family’s oil-refining facilities in Gujarat, where more than 150,000 animals have reportedly been amassed since 2022. Vantara boasts high welfare standards for animals in its care, including facilities such as an elephant hydrotherapy pool, where more than 260 elephants can also receive oil therapies and Ayurvedic massage.

But conservation groups have repeatedly questioned how such a vast number of species, many of which are endangered, were gathered so quickly. Last year, India’s supreme court cleared the zoo’s operators of any wrongdoing.

A subsequent Cites fact-finding mission looking into the zoo raised concerns about India’s compliance with international rules on animal imports in 2025. It recommended temporary restrictions on India, although the recommendation was later withdrawn.

Its November 2025 report said: “There is a need for caution to ensure that imports of large numbers of animals by these facilities are not inadvertently creating a demand for illegally sourced animals.”

blocks.caption: British officials were invited to visit the controversial zoo.  Photograph: P Paranjpe/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: In May, officials from the UK’s Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) met a representative from Vantara and the US lobbyist firm Checkmate Government Relations, founded by Ches McDowell, a hunting friend of Donald Trump Jr.

Before the meeting, internal briefing documents said Checkmate was “seeking to persuade the UK to take a more sympathetic view of India’s handling of imports to Vantara and of Checkmate’s argument that responsibility for verifying legality sits primarily with exporting or re-exporting parties rather than with India as importer”.

blocks.caption: Vantara boasts high welfare standards for animals in its care. Photograph: P Paranjpe/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: During the meeting, the Vantara representative invited UK officials to visit the zoo – an invitation that was subsequently declined to ensure the impartiality of the UK’s Cites chair role.

After the meeting, a representative from another lobbying firm, Atlas Strategy, working on behalf of Vantara, approached the then secretary of state, Emma Reynolds, and then nature minister, Mary Creagh, also raising the prospect of a visit to the zoo.
When Reynolds asked for advice, a note was issued recommending that ministers did not engage formally with Vantara.

The government documents also reveal concerns about an application by Vantara to import falcons and falcon hybrids, after an unnamed organisation made a £50,000 “donation” to a breeder in the UK, whose identity was also not disclosed. British Cites officials classified the transaction as commercial, according to the documents. The falcons were not exported to India.

A spokesperson for Vantara said it had not imported falcons from the UK, nor had the zoo hired or paid a lobbying firm. It is understood that Checkmate and Altas Strategy were working pro bono for Vantara and not required to register with the Office of the Registrar of Consultant Lobbyists.

blocks.caption: Elephants at a veterinary hospital in Vantara. Photograph: Punit Paranjpe/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: After recent scrutiny, Vantara has sought to “reset” its activities by voluntarily suspending animal imports for a year and hiring John Scanlon, a former Cites chief, to oversee its operations. In an interview with the Sunday Times this year, Ambani said he only brought animals to Vantara legally to ensure their welfare, mentioning a group of hippos he had saved from a hunting lodge in South Africa and jackass penguins saved from a shopping centre in Qatar.
“I think since I was a baby I have been taking care of animals. It’s always been a passion,” he said.

Vantara was used to host Ambani’s lavish pre-wedding celebrations in 2024, which were attended by celebrity guests and politicians. In September, Newcastle University awarded the oil heir a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship”, sparking a backlash from conservationists.

A Defra spokesperson said: “The UK has strict rules in place to protect endangered species and ensuring international wildlife trade is legal and sustainable, with every application assessed individually against internationally agreed and domestic requirements.”
Find more age of extinction coverage here, and follow the biodiversity reporters Rebecca Ratcliffe, Phoebe Weston and Patrick Greenfield in the Guardian app for more nature coverage.

articles.title: New York child dies from measles in state’s first fatal case in 30 years
articles.summary:
New York governor says case is ‘devastating reminder of what’s at stake’ when vaccine protections are eroded

A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking…

blocks.text: A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the state’s first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday.
The child died in Lewis county, about 93 miles (150km) north of Syracuse, New York governor Kathy Hochul said.
“I am heartbroken to learn that a child in Lewis County has died after contracting measles,” Hochul said in a statement.

Hochul linked the death to the federal government’s stance on immunisation, saying: “This is New York’s first measles-related death in 30 years, a devastating reminder of what’s at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”
Measles is a highly contagious virus that can cause serious health complications. Although rare, deaths from measles occur in approximately one to three patients per 1,000 cases.

The US stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the US this year, but state health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported six deaths this year.
Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring states and in rural areas of New York.
The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.
The CDC reported 4,588 cases of measles across the country in 2026 as of late October – more than double the tally for 2025.
Pennsylvania alone reported 1,338 cases on the same day. The CDC also reported large outbreaks in South Carolina and Utah, both of which are reporting more than 500 cases.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US department of health and human services (HHS), has faced criticism for his comments on some vaccines, and made sweeping changes to vaccination policy, including cutting childhood immunisation recommendations by a third.
With Associated Press

articles.title: North Korea denies role in record Binance hack, calls US charge 'provocation'
articles.summary: Kim Yo Jong dismissed FBI claims that North Korean hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance, as the exchange began reopening withdrawals on more networks.

image.caption: Binance said it replaced most of the stolen assets out of its own fundsImage: Sk Mijanur Rahaman/imageBROKER/picture alliance

blocks.text: North Korea has hit back at US accusations that its hackers drained more than $6 billion (more than 5.36 billion euros) from cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, called the charge "a grave political provocation," according to state media agency KCNA.
Kim described the US claim as "absurd rhetoric and nothing new.”
What do we know about the hacking?
The accusation came from the FBI, which blamed a state-tied hacking group called TraderTraitor over the weekend.

This was reportedly the biggest crypto-exchange heist on record, well above the roughly $1.5 billion Bybit raid in 2025, which was also attributed to North Korean hackers. TRM Labs linked the attack to the same group and said it shifted most of the money out within 20 minutes, German news agency DPA reported.
Cryptocurrency giant Binance hit by $6.3 billion hack
Kim Yo Jong said Pyongyang now had "issues to reconsider" because of Washington's hostility.

North Korea has so far stayed silent on Trump's overtures about reviving summit talks. Analysts in Seoul told Reuters news agency the speed of the denial points to concern that Washington could step up efforts to cut off a funding source widely believed to bankroll arms development.
Is Binance working again?

Separately, Binance announced Monday that withdrawals will restart for additional assets across several blockchains, among them Binance Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Sui, from 04:00 GMT Tuesday.
Selected tokens on Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base are part of the same rollout.
Binance said it replaced most of the stolen assets out of its own funds.

articles.title: US strikes Iran ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.

blocks.text: The US has launched strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials have told CBS, the BBC's US partner.
Iranian state news agency IRNA reported several explosions on the island on Monday.
The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to the Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.
The BBC has contacted US Central Command (Centcom), the part of the US military responsible for operations in the Middle East, for comment.
It comes ahead of the US midterm elections, which will determine whether the Republicans or Democrats control Congress.
Trump has been facing falling polling numbers and pressure from within his party to end the war, which began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in February.
Earlier on Monday, he told reporters that he was in "no rush" to ramp up strikes on Iran.

"One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially," he told news outlet Axios. "They have no money, no gasoline and their people are getting very tired of it."
He also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe", a site linked to Iran's nuclear programme, in an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterm elections.
This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump added.

There has been mounting speculation in the last few days that the US may resume significant strikes in Iran again after the midterms. But asked by a reporter on Monday if that was the case, Trump said "no".
Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that "very intensive" talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios "more than ever before" and that it was up to the US to choose between a "wise path" of negotiation or the "mistake of military aggression".
